mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions and reduced corporate investment demand.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no significant negative returns occur when the trigger is active (t-test p > 0.05), or the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the pre-trigger mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in new job openings (indirect proxy via INDPRO) signals labor market weakness that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 20 out of 30 such triggered windows, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction rank IC exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above trend for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: Across 10 such cycles, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal's IC is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as it signals weak manufacturing momentum and reduced earnings expectations.
failure_condition: In 8 out of 10 such contractions, the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the IC is above 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return becomes positive as expectations of future rate cuts support equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 40 such windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the IC exceeds 0.12.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and a decline in housing starts (implied via HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as it reflects weak labor market and housing market conditions.
failure_condition: In 15 such events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction rank IC is above 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time surge in retail sales ( proxy via GDPC1 > previous_month * 1.05 ) followed by two consecutive months of normal GDP growth predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals demand resilience.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous_month * 1.05 AND GDPC1_2m > previous_month * 1.02 AND GDPC1_3m > previous_month * 1.00
regime_hint: Retail demand shock resolving into growth
failure_condition: Across 12 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the IC is below 0.08.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence ( proxy via a composite of RSAFS and HOUST both below trend for 4 consecutive months ) predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns as it reflects persistent softening in business conditions.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < trend_4m AND HOUST < trend_4m for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 such 4-month softening periods, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction rank IC exceeds 0.15.
